headline: Losses narrow as operations swing profitable on deliveries

kpis.label: Operating income (loss)
kpis.delta: swung to profit from a $176M loss

summary_short: Boeing's Q2 2026 revenue rose 8.0% y/y to $24.56B on 171 commercial deliveries, with the GAAP loss narrowing to $0.67/share from $0.92 and operating income swinging to a $156M profit from a $176M loss a year earlier.
summary_long: Revenue rose 8% y/y to $24.56B on 171 commercial deliveries. Commercial Airplanes margin improved to -2.7% from -5.1% on higher deliveries and mix; Defense, Space & Security swung to a $15M operating loss on a $280M VC-25B charge for added production/certification resources; Global Services margin fell to 18.1% on the Digital Aviation Solutions divestiture and unfavorable mix. Consolidated operating income swung to $156M from a $176M loss; GAAP diluted loss per share narrowed to $0.67 from $0.92. Cash and short-term investments fell to $20.0B from $20.9B on debt repayments; consolidated debt eased to $45.9B. Backlog hit a record $715B. No formal quarterly guidance was issued; management flagged more work ahead in H2.

drivers.explanation: CEO Kelly Ortberg cited more stable operations, on-plan certification programs, and a sustained focus on safety, quality, and on-time performance as building momentum, while flagging more work ahead in H2.

Growth reflects 171 commercial deliveries (+14% y/y), 246 net orders, and higher volume across Commercial Airplanes, Defense Space & Security, and Global Services, per the release's own results summary.

Commercial Airplanes' operating loss narrowed on higher deliveries, favorable mix, and improved performance; Defense, Space & Security swung to a small loss on a $280M VC-25B charge for added production/certification resources.
The 1.4pt margin gain is fully explained by the operating-income swing (to +$156M from -$176M) against similarly-sized revenue, matching the release's own stated Table 1 delta.
The per-share loss narrowed as net loss to common shareholders fell to $530M from $697M, while diluted shares rose to 790.6M from 756.6M — the loss reduction outweighed added dilution.
The narrower net loss reflects the operating-income swing to profit and lower interest expense ($600M vs $710M), partly offset by a drop in other income, net, to $79M from $325M.
The release attributes the quarter's decline directly to debt repayments, partially offset by cash flow generated in the quarter.
